source_units.text: A song of the ascents. To the Lord, when I was afflicted, I cried, and He heard me.
Lord, rescue my soul from unjust lips and from a deceitful tongue.
What might be given to you, and what might be added to you, against a deceitful tongue?
The mighty one’s sharpened arrows, with desert coals.
Alas for me, for my sojourn has been prolonged; I have encamped among the tents of Kedar.
My soul has sojourned a long time.
With those who hate peace I was peaceable; whenever I spoke to them, they fought me without cause.
A song of the ascents. I lifted my eyes to the mountains. From where will my help come?
My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Do not give your foot over to shaking, and may your Keeper not slumber.
Behold, the One guarding Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The Lord will guard you; the Lord is your shelter at your right hand.
By day the sun will not scorch you, nor the moon by night.
The Lord will guard you from all evil; He will guard your soul.
The Lord will guard your coming in and your going out, from now and for ever.
A song of the ascents. I rejoiced over those who said to me, “We will go to the Lord’s house.”
Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, being built as a city whose common sharing is together,
for there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord—a testimony for Israel— to give thanks to the Lord’s name.
For there thrones sat for judgment, thrones over David’s house.
Ask, then, for the things that bring Jerusalem peace, and prosperity for those who love you.
May there be peace within your strength, and prosperity within your fortified towers.
For the sake of my brothers and neighbors, I was speaking peace concerning you.
For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things for you.
A song of the ascents. To Thee I lifted my eyes, Thou who dwellest in heaven.
Behold, as slaves’ eyes turn to their masters’ hands, as a slave woman’s eyes turn to her mistress’s hands, so our eyes turn to the Lord our God, until He has compassion on us.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with contempt to excess,
Our soul has been filled beyond measure. Reproach for those who prosper, and contempt for the proud.
A song of the ascents. Had the Lord not been among us— let Israel now say—
had the Lord not been among us when people rose against us,
then they would have swallowed us alive when their fury was kindled against us.
Then the water drowned us; our soul passed through a torrent.
Then our soul passed through the irresistible water.
Blessed be the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth.
Our soul was rescued like a little bird from the trap of hunters; the trap was shattered, and we were rescued.
Our help is in the Lord’s name, who made heaven and earth.
A song of the ascents. Those trusting in the Lord are like Mount Zion; the one dwelling in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Mountains are around her, and the Lord is around His people, from now and for ever.
For He will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous may not stretch out their hands in lawlessness.
Do good, Lord, to the good and to those upright in heart.
But those turning aside into tangled ways— the Lord will lead them away with workers of lawlessness. Peace upon Israel.
A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”
The Lord has done great things with us; we became glad.
Turn back our captivity, Lord, like torrents in the south.
Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.
Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.
A song of the ascents. For Solomon. Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.
It is vain for you to rise early, to get up after sitting down, you who eat bread of pain, when He gives sleep to His beloved ones.
Behold, sons are the Lord’s inheritance, the reward of the fruit of the womb.
Like arrows in a mighty man’s hand, so are the sons of those who have been cast out.
Happy is the person who will fill his desire with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies at the gate.
A song of the ascents. Happy are all who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways.
You will eat the labors of your wrists; happy are you, and it will be well with you.
Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.
Behold, thus will the person be blessed who fears the Lord.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see Jerusalem’s good things all the days of your life.
And may you see sons of your sons. Peace upon Israel.
A song of the ascents. Many times they fought against me from my youth— let Israel now say—
many times they fought against me from my youth, and indeed they did not prevail over me.
On my back sinners worked; they prolonged their lawlessness.
The righteous Lord cut apart the necks of sinners.
May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turn backward.
May they become like grass on roofs, which dried up before it was pulled out,
with which no reaper has filled his hand, nor the one gathering sheaves his bosom,
And passersby have not said, “The Lord’s blessing be upon you; we have blessed you in the Lord’s name.”
A song of the ascents. From the depths I have cried unto Thee, Lord.
Lord, hear my voice; let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my petition.
If Thou dost closely watch lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will withstand?
For with Thee is atonement.
Because of Thy law I waited for Thee, Lord; my soul waited for Thy word.
My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
For with the Lord is mercy, and with Him is abundant redemption,
And He will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds.
A song of the ascents. For David. Lord, my heart was not exalted, nor were my eyes raised high; I did not walk among great things nor among wonders beyond me.
If I was not humble-minded, but exalted my soul— like the weaned child upon its mother, like repayment upon my soul.
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and for ever.
A song of the ascents. Remember David, Lord, and all his gentleness,
how he swore to the Lord, vowed to the God of Jacob:
“I will not enter the dwelling of my house, nor climb onto my bed’s couch;
I will not give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, or rest to my temples,
until I find a place for the Lord, a dwelling for the God of Jacob.”
Behold, we heard of her in Ephrathah; we found her in the plains of the forest.
We will enter His dwelling places; we will bow toward the place where His feet stood.
Rise, Lord, to Thy rest, Thou and the ark of Thy holiness.
Thy priests will clothe themselves in righteousness, and Thy holy ones will exult.
For the sake of David Thy slave, do not turn away the face of Thine anointed.
The Lord swore truth to David, and He will certainly not annul it: “From the fruit of your belly I will set one on your throne.
If your sons keep My covenant and these testimonies of Mine that I will teach them, their sons too will sit for ever on your throne.”
For the Lord chose Zion; He selected her as His dwelling:
“This is My rest for age upon age; here I will dwell, for I selected her.
I will surely bless her game; I will satisfy her poor with loaves.
I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her holy ones will surely exult.
There I will make a horn spring up for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed.
I will clothe his enemies with shame, but upon him My holy sign will blossom.”
A song of the ascents. For David. Behold, what is good or what is delightful except for brothers to dwell together?
Like ointment upon the head, descending upon the beard, Aaron’s beard, descending upon the border of his garment;
Like Hermon’s dew descending upon Zion’s mountains; for there the Lord commanded the blessing and life for ever.
A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.
By night lift your hands toward the holy places and bless the Lord.
The Lord will bless you from Zion, who made heaven and earth.
Hallelujah! Praise the Lord’s name; praise the Lord, slaves,
you who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of our God’s house.
Praise the Lord, for the Lord is good; make music to His name, for it is beautiful.
For the Lord chose Jacob for Himself, Israel as His special possession.
For I knew that the Lord is great, and our Lord is above all the gods.
Everything the Lord willed, He did, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deeps.
He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.
He struck Egypt’s firstborn, from man to beast.
He sent out signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, upon Pharaoh and all his slaves.
He struck many nations and killed powerful kings,
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all Canaan’s kingdoms.
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
Lord, Thy name is for ever; Lord, Thy memorial is from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge His people and be comforted concerning His slaves.
The nations’ idols are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth but will not speak; they have eyes but will not see.

They have ears but will not listen; they have noses but will not smell; they have hands but will not touch; they have feet but will not walk; they will not sound in their throat, for there is no breath in their mouth.
May those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them.
House of Israel, bless the Lord; house of Aaron, bless the Lord.
House of Levi, bless the Lord; you who fear the Lord, bless the Lord.
Blessed be the Lord from Zion, He who dwells in Jerusalem.
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for He is kind; for His mercy is for ever.
Give thanks to the God of gods; for His mercy is for ever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who alone does great wonders; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who made the heavens with understanding; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who made the earth firm upon the waters; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who alone made great lights; for His mercy is for ever.
the sun for authority over the day; for His mercy is for ever.
the moon and stars for authority over the night; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who struck Egypt with their firstborn; for His mercy is for ever.
And to Him who brought Israel out from their midst; for His mercy is for ever.
with a mighty hand and a raised arm; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who divided the Red Sea into divisions; for His mercy is for ever.
And to Him who led Israel through its midst; for His mercy is for ever.
And to Him who shook Pharaoh and his force into the Red Sea; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who led His people through the wilderness; for His mercy is for ever. To Him who brought water out of a sheer rock; for His mercy is for ever.
To Him who struck great kings; for His mercy is for ever.
And to Him who killed mighty kings; for His mercy is for ever.
Sihon king of the Amorites; for His mercy is for ever.
and Og king of Bashan; for His mercy is for ever.
And to Him who gave their land as an inheritance; for His mercy is for ever.
an inheritance to Israel His slave; for His mercy is for ever.
For in our humiliation the Lord remembered us; for His mercy is for ever.
And He redeemed us from our enemies; for His mercy is for ever.
He gives food to all flesh; for His mercy is for ever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven; for His mercy is for ever. Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for His mercy is for ever.

context_units.text: The Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the sea creature’s belly three days and three nights.
Jonah prayed to the Lord his God from the sea creature’s belly,
and said: “In my affliction I cried to the Lord my God, and He listened to me. From the belly of Hades Thou didst hear the voice of my cry.
Thou didst cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers encircled me. All Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.
I said, ‘I have been thrust away from Thine eyes. Shall I again look toward Thy holy sanctuary?’
Water poured around me up to my life; the uttermost abyss encircled me; my head sank into clefts of mountains.
I descended into a land whose bars are everlasting restraints; and let the ruin of my life rise up, Lord my God.
As my life was failing me, I remembered the Lord; may my prayer come to Thee, into Thy holy sanctuary.
Those who guard vain and false things abandoned their mercy.
But I, with a voice of praise and thanksgiving, will sacrifice to Thee. Whatever I vowed I will repay to Thee, for deliverance to the Lord!”
The sea creature was commanded, and it cast Jonah out onto dry land.
For the end, concerning the eighth. A psalm of David.
Save me, Lord, for the holy one is gone; for truths have become few among the sons of men.
Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart.
May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and a boastful tongue—
those who said, “We will magnify our tongue; our lips are our own; who is our lord?”
“Because of the misery of the poor and because of the groaning of the needy, now I will arise,” says the Lord. “I will set him in salvation; I will speak openly in him.”
The sayings of the Lord are pure sayings, silver tried by fire, tested in the earth, purified sevenfold.
Thou, Lord, wilt keep us and preserve us from this generation and for ever.
The ungodly walk around; according to Thy height, Thou heldest the sons of men in high regard.
Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.
In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; take the lead in honoring one another;
do not be slack in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;
rejoice in hope; persevere in affliction; persist in prayer;
share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
Have the same mind toward one another. Do not set your minds on lofty things, but associate with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own eyes.
Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is honorable before all people.
If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but make room for wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
And I said, May it be, Lord! For I will place you among children and give you a chosen land, an inheritance of God Almighty of nations. I said, You will call Me Father and will not turn away from Me.
But as a woman deals faithlessly with the one living with her, so the house of Israel dealt faithlessly with Me, says the Lord.
A voice was heard from lips, the weeping and supplication of Israel’s children, because they acted unjustly in their ways and forgot their holy God.
Return, returning children, and I will heal your fractures. Behold, we will be Thy servants, because Thou art the Lord our God.
Truly the hills and the power of the mountains were false; but through the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.
Shame consumed our fathers’ labors from our youth: their sheep and calves, their sons and daughters.
We lay down in our shame, and our dishonor covered us, because we sinned before our God, we and our fathers, from our youth until this day, and did not obey the voice of the Lord our God.
Bless our God, nations, and cause the sound of His praise to be heard,
He who set my soul in life and did not give my feet over to shaking.
For Thou didst test us, God; Thou didst try us by fire as silver is tried by fire.
Thou broughtest us into the trap; Thou didst place afflictions upon our back.
Thou madest human beings mount our heads; we passed through fire and water, and Thou broughtest us out to refreshment.
Ahab sent throughout all Israel and gathered all the prophets at Mount Carmel.
Elijah came near them all and said to them, “How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, follow Him; if Baal is, follow him.” The people did not answer a word.
Elijah said to the people, “I remain as the Lord’s prophet utterly alone, but Baal’s prophets are four hundred fifty men, and the grove’s prophets are four hundred.

Let them give us two oxen. Let them choose one for themselves, cut it in pieces, and place it on the wood, but put no fire under it. I will prepare the other ox, but I will certainly put no fire under it.
Cry out in the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord my God. The God who answers by fire—He is God.” All the people answered, “The proposal you have spoken is good.”
Elijah said to the prophets of shame, “Choose one young bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many. Call on the name of your god, but put no fire under it.”

They took the young bull and prepared it. They called on Baal’s name from morning until noon, saying, “Hear us, Baal, hear us!” But there was no voice and no hearing. They ran about on the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, “Call with a loud voice, for he is a god! He has chattering to do; perhaps he is also conducting business, or perhaps he is asleep and will get up!”
They called with a loud voice and cut themselves according to their custom with knives and lances, until blood poured over them.

They prophesied until the late afternoon had passed. When it was time for the sacrifice to go up and there was no voice, Elijah the Tishbite spoke to the prophets of offenses: “Move away now, and I will prepare my burnt offering.” They moved away and departed.
Elijah said to the people, “Come near me.” All the people came near him.
Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of Israel’s tribes, as the Lord had spoken to him, saying, “Israel will be your name.”
He built the stones in the Lord’s name and repaired the altar that had been demolished. He made a trench around the altar, holding two metretes of seed.
He piled the split wood on the altar he had made, cut the burnt offering in pieces, placed it on the split wood, and piled it on the altar.

He said, “Bring me four water jars of water and pour it on the burnt offering and the split wood.” They did so. He said, “Do it a second time,” and they did it a second time. He said, “Do it a third time,” and they did it a third time.
The water ran around the altar, and they filled the trench with water.

Elijah cried out to heaven and said, “Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, hear me, Lord! Hear me this day with fire, and let all this people know that Thou art the Lord, the God of Israel, and I am Thy servant, and that I have done these works because of Thee.
Hear me, Lord! Hear me with fire, and let this people know that Thou art the Lord God, and that Thou hast turned this people’s heart backward.”
Fire from the Lord fell from heaven and consumed the burnt offering, the split wood, and the water in the trench; the fire licked up the stones and the dust.
All the people fell on their faces and said, “Truly the Lord is God! He is God!”
The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; Thou art the One who restores my inheritance to me.
Measuring cords fell for me among the best places; indeed, my inheritance is the best for me.
I will bless the Lord, who gave me understanding; indeed, even until night my kidneys disciplined me.
I kept seeing the Lord before me continually, because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.
Therefore my heart rejoiced, and my tongue exulted; indeed, even my flesh will dwell in hope,
for Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades, nor let Thy holy one see corruption.
Thou madest known to me ways of life; Thou wilt fill me with gladness in Thy presence; pleasures are at Thy right hand for ever.
Listen to me, islands, and attend, nations. “After a long time it will stand,” says the Lord. From my mother’s belly He called my name,
and made my mouth like a sharp sword. In the shelter of His hand He hid me; He made me a chosen arrow and sheltered me in His quiver.
He said to me, “You are My slave, Israel, and in you I will be glorified.”
I said, “I toiled in vain and gave my strength to futility and nothing. Therefore my judgment is with the Lord, and my toil before my God.”
And now thus says the Lord, who formed me from the belly as His slave to gather Jacob and Israel to Him—I will be gathered and glorified before the Lord, and my God will be my strength—

and He said to me, “It is a great thing for you to be called My servant, to establish Jacob’s tribes and bring back Israel’s dispersion. Behold, I have appointed you as a covenant for a race, a light for nations, so that you may bring salvation to the earth’s extremity.”

Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s God: “Sanctify the one who despises his own life, the one abhorred by nations—the slaves of rulers. Kings will see him and rise; rulers will bow to him because of the Lord, for Israel’s Holy One is faithful, and I chose you.”
Thus says the Lord: “At an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. I gave you as a covenant for nations, to establish the earth and inherit a desolate inheritance,
saying to those in bonds, ‘Come out,’ and telling those in darkness to be revealed. They will be fed along all their roads, with pasture along every path.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, nor will scorching heat or the sun strike them. Rather, the One showing them mercy will comfort them and lead them through springs of water.
I will make every mountain into a road and every path into pasture for them.
Behold, these come from afar, these from the north and these from the sea, and others from the Persians’ land.”
Rejoice, heavens, and let earth exult! Let mountains burst out in joy and hills in righteousness, for God had mercy on His people and comforted His people’s lowly ones.

And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you, and find you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Blessed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord your God deliver your enemies who rise against you, crushed before your face. By one way shall they come out against you, and by seven ways shall they flee before you.
The Lord send His blessing upon you in your storerooms, and in all that you put your hand unto, upon the land which the Lord your God gives you.
The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

The Lord open unto you His good treasure, heaven, to give rain unto your land in its season, and to bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend unto many nations, but you shall not borrow; and you shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
The Lord your God make you the head, and not the tail; and you shall be above, and not beneath, if you hearken unto the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day to keep and do.
You shall not turn aside from any of the words which I command you this day, to the right hand or to the left, to go after other gods and serve them.
The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah son of Amos concerning Judea and Jerusalem.
In the last days the Lord’s mountain and God’s house will be clearly visible on the summits of the mountains and be raised above the hills; all the nations will come to it,

and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people. They will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles. Nation will no longer take sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk by the Lord’s light!
You shall keep the Feast of Tents seven days, when you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your winepress.

And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male slave, and your female slave, and the Levite, and the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow within your cities.

You shall keep a feast for seven days unto the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for Himself; and if the Lord your God blesses you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, you shall rejoice.

Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
but every man according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you.
And say to this people: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have set before your face the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine; whoever goes out to join the Chaldeans who have shut you in will live, and his life will be spoil, and he will live.
Because I have fixed My face upon this city for evils and not for good things. It will be handed into Babylon’s king’s hands, and he will burn it down with fire.
House of Judah’s king, hear the Lord’s word.

House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.
Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Sor, the level land, you who say, Who will frighten us? Or who will enter our dwelling?
And I will kindle a fire in her woodland, and it will consume everything around her.
As He was already drawing near the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works they had seen,
saying, “Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!”
And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, rebuke Thy disciples.”
And He answered, “I tell you, if these fall silent, the stones will cry out.”
As He drew near and saw the city, He wept over it,
saying, “If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will build a siege barrier around you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
They will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and will not leave stone upon stone within you, because you did not know the time of your visitation.”
Because you became abandoned and hated, with no one helping, I will make you an everlasting exultation, joy for generations upon generations.
You will suck the nations’ milk and eat kings’ wealth. You will know that I am the Lord who saves and delivers you, Israel’s God.
Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, instead of iron silver, instead of wood bronze, and instead of stones iron. I will appoint your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
Injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Engraving.
The sun will not be your light by day, nor will the rising moon light your night. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light and God your glory.
For your sun will not set, and your moon will not fail. The Lord will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be fulfilled.
Your people will all be righteous, and they will inherit the land for ever, guarding the planting, the works of His hands, for glory.
The fewest will become thousands, and the least a great nation. I, the Lord, will gather them at the proper time.
Jesus spoke these things, and, lifting His eyes to heaven, said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Thy Son, so that the Son may glorify Thee,
just as Thou gavest Him authority over all flesh, so that He may give eternal life to them—to all that Thou hast given Him.
And this is eternal life: that they know Thee, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom Thou didst send.
I glorified Thee on the earth, having completed the work that Thou hast given Me to do.
And now, Father, glorify Me with Thyself, with the glory that I had with Thee before the world existed.
“I revealed Thy name to the people whom Thou gavest Me out of the world. They were Thine, and Thou gavest them to Me, and they have kept Thy word.
Now they have known that everything Thou hast given Me is from Thee,
because the words that Thou gavest Me I have given them; and they received them and truly knew that I came forth from Thee, and believed that Thou didst send Me.
I ask concerning them. I do not ask concerning the world, but concerning those whom Thou hast given Me, because they are Thine;
and all that is Mine is Thine, and what is Thine is Mine, and I have been glorified in them.
And I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to Thee. Holy Father, keep them in Thy name, which Thou hast given Me, so that they may be one just as We are.
When I was with them, I kept them in Thy name, which Thou hast given Me, and guarded them; and not one of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to Thee, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have My joy made full within themselves.
I have given them Thy word, and the world hated them, because they are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
I do not ask that Thou take them out of the world, but that Thou keep them from the evil one.
They are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
Sanctify them in the truth; Thy word is truth.
Just as Thou didst send Me into the world, I also sent them into the world;
and for their sake I sanctify Myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth.
When Sanaballat heard that we were building the wall, it displeased him. He became very angry and laughed at the Jews.
He said before his brothers, “Is this the strength of Somoron, that these Jews are building their own city?”
Tobias the Ammanite came beside him, and they said to one another, “Surely they will not sacrifice or eat in their place? Will not a fox climb up and pull down their stone wall?”
Hear, our God, for we have become an object of mockery. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them over to mockery in a land of captivity,
and do not cover over lawlessness.
And we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, those who are called according to purpose.
Because those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He might be firstborn among many brothers;
and those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, these He also glorified.
What, then, shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
He who did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over for us all, how will He not also graciously give us all things with Him?
Who will bring a charge against God’s chosen ones? God is the One who justifies.
Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died—more than that, was raised—who is also at God’s right hand, who also intercedes for us.
Who will separate us from Christ’s love? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
Just as it is written, “For Thy sake we are put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.”
But in all these things we more than conquer through the One who loved us.
For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither things present nor things to come nor powers,
neither height nor depth nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from God’s love in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Listen, son, to your father’s discipline, and do not reject your mother’s ordinances,
for you will receive a crown of graces for your head and a golden collar around your neck.
Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray; do not agree if they invite you, saying,
Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.
For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.
For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
For the end. Concerning those who will be changed. Of David.
Save me, God, for waters have entered as far as my soul.
I was stuck in the mud of the depth, with no firm ground; I entered the sea’s depths, and a tempest drowned me.
I grew weary crying out; my throat became hoarse; my eyes failed from hoping in my God.
More numerous than the hairs on my head became those hating me without cause; my enemies pursuing me unjustly became strong. What I did not plunder, I was then repaying.
But now thus says the Lord God who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel: “Do not fear, for I redeemed you. I called you by your name; you are Mine.
Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.
For I am the Lord your God, Israel’s Holy One, who saves you. I made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Soene on your behalf.
Since you became honored before Me, you were glorified, and I loved you. I will give many people on your behalf and rulers for your head.
Do not fear, for I am with you. From the east I will bring your offspring, and from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, ‘Bring them,’ and to the southwest, ‘Do not hinder. Bring My sons from a distant land and My daughters from the earth’s extremities,
all who are called by My name.’ For in My glory I fashioned him, formed him, and made him,
Job continued and said in his prelude:
“Who might place me in a month of former days, when God guarded me?
As when His lamp shone above my head, when by His light I walked in darkness,
when I was weighty in my ways, when God made an inspection of my house,
when I was flourishing abundantly, and my children were around me,
when my roads were flooded with butter, and my mountains were flooded with milk,
when I went out early in the city, and my chair was set in the squares.
Young men saw me and hid, and all the elders stood.
Powerful men stopped speaking, placing a finger upon their mouths.
Those who heard called me blessed, and their tongues clung to their throats.
For an ear heard and called me blessed, and an eye that saw me turned aside.
For I rescued a poor person from a powerful man’s hand and helped an orphan who had no helper.
May the blessing of the perishing come upon me, and a widow’s mouth blessed me.
I had clothed myself with righteousness, and I wrapped myself in justice like a double cloak.
I was an eye for the blind and a foot for the lame.
I was a father to the powerless, and I traced out a case I did not know.
I crushed the molars of unjust people and tore the plunder from between their teeth.
I said, ‘My age will grow old; like the trunk of a palm I will live a long time.
Son, if you act as guarantor for your friend, you will give your hand over to an enemy.
For a man’s own lips are a strong trap, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
Son, do what I command you and save yourself—for through your friend you have come into evil men’s hands. Go without growing slack, and press the friend for whom you acted as guarantor.
Give no sleep to your eyes, nor doze with your eyelids,
so that you may save yourself like a gazelle from snares and like a bird from a trap.
Go to the ant, sluggard; see its ways and emulate them, and become wiser than it.
For although it has no cultivated field, and has no one forcing it, and is under no master,
it prepares its food in summer and makes abundant provision at harvest.
Or go to the bee and learn how industrious she is, and how nobly she performs her work,
whose labors kings and private people use for health; she is desired by everyone and held in esteem.
Although weak in bodily strength, she was advanced because she honored wisdom.
How long will you remain lying down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
For the end. Concerning the sons of Korah. A psalm concerning hidden things.
Our God is refuge and strength, a helper in the afflictions that have greatly overtaken us.
Therefore we will not fear when the earth is disturbed and mountains are displaced into the hearts of seas.
Their waters roared and were disturbed; the mountains were disturbed at his might. Diapsalma.
The river’s rushing streams gladden God’s city; the Most High sanctified His dwelling.
God is in her midst; she will not be shaken; God will help her toward morning.
Nations were disturbed; kingdoms bent; He gave His voice; the earth was shaken.
The Lord of powers is with us; Jacob’s God is our supporter. Diapsalma.
Come, see the Lord’s works, the wonders He has set upon the earth.
Bringing wars to an end as far as the earth’s limits, He will shatter a bow and break a weapon apart and burn shields in fire.
“Cease your activity and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, exalted in the earth.”
The Lord of powers is with us; Jacob’s God is our supporter.
I lifted my eyes and saw: look, a man with a land-measuring cord in his hand!
I said to him, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long.”
Look, the angel speaking within me was standing, and another angel was going out to meet him,
and said to him, “Run and speak to that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited fruitfully because of the multitude of people and animals within her.
I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”
“Oh! Oh! Flee from the northern land,” says the Lord, “because I will gather you from the four winds of heaven,” says the Lord.
Escape safely to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon!
For thus says the Lord Almighty: “After glory He has sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you is like one touching the pupil of his eye.
Look, I am bringing My hand against them, and they will become spoils for those serving them; you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me.”
“Delight and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell within you,” says the Lord.
Many nations will take refuge with the Lord on that day and become His people. They will dwell within you, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
The Lord will inherit Judah as His portion on the holy land and again choose Jerusalem.
Let all flesh be reverent before the Lord, for He has risen from His holy clouds.
The Lord will pity Jacob and again choose Israel; they will rest upon their land, and the resident foreigner will be added to them and added to Jacob’s house,

and nations will take them and bring them into their place; they will inherit and multiply upon God’s land as male and female slaves. Those who took them captive will be captives, and those who ruled them will be ruled.
On that day God will give you rest from pain, your wrath and the harsh slavery in which you served them,
and you will take up this lament against Babylon’s king and say on that day, “How the one who made demands has rested, and the taskmaster rested!
God shattered the sinners’ yoke, the rulers’ yoke;
having struck a nation in wrath with an incurable blow, striking a nation with a blow of anger that did not spare,
he rested confidently. The whole earth cries out with gladness,
and Lebanon’s trees rejoiced over you, and Lebanon’s cedar: ‘Since you have fallen asleep, the one cutting us has not come up.’
A psalm of Asaph. How good God is to Israel, to those upright in heart!
But my feet were almost shaken; my steps were nearly poured out.
For I envied the lawless, beholding sinners’ peace,
Do not be deceived; God is not mocked. For whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
For the one who sows into his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in the proper season we will reap, if we do not give up.
So then, as we have opportunity, let us do good to everyone, especially to those of the household of faith.
See with what large letters I have written to you in my own hand.
All who want to make a good outward show in the flesh compel you to receive circumcision, only so that they may not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For even those who receive circumcision do not themselves keep the law, but they want you to receive circumcision so that they may boast in your flesh.
But may I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but a new creation does.
And as many as will keep in step with this rule, peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God.
From now on, let no one cause me trouble, for I carry the marks of Jesus in my body.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.
Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will return Jacob’s deportees and have mercy on his captivity. A city will be built upon its height, and the sanctuary will sit according to its judgment.
And singers and the sound of people playing will come out from them. I will increase them, and they will certainly not be diminished.
And their sons will enter as formerly, and their testimonies will be set upright before Me. I will visit those afflicting them.
And stronger ones of his will be over them, and his ruler will come out from him. I will gather them, and they will return to Me. For who is this who gave his heart to return to Me? says the Lord.
Because the Lord’s anger went out furious; swirling anger went out and will come upon the ungodly.
The anger of the Lord’s fury will certainly not turn back until He acts and establishes His heart’s undertaking. At the end of the days you will know these things.
Then Bildad the Shuhite replied:
“How long will you speak these things? The breath of your mouth is full of words.
Will the Lord do wrong in judging, or will the Maker of all disturb what is right?
If your sons sinned before Him, He sent them into the power of their lawlessness.
But rise early to the Lord Almighty in supplication.
If you are pure and true, He will hear your supplication and restore to you a righteous way of life.
Then your first things will be few, but your last things beyond telling.
For inquire of the former generation; search out the family of the fathers.
For we are of yesterday and do not know; our life on earth is a shadow.
Will these not teach you and tell you, and bring words out of the heart?
Does papyrus flourish without water, or will a rush grow tall without a drink?
While it is still on its root and unharvested, does not every plant wither before it drinks?
So, then, will be the latter end of all who forget the Lord; for the hope of an ungodly person will perish.
For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn into a spider’s web.
If he props up his house, it will certainly not stand; when he takes hold of it, it will certainly not endure.
For he is moist beneath the sun, and his shoot will come out of his decay.
He lies upon a heap of stones and will live among pebbles.
If it swallows him up, the place will disown him. Have you not seen such things?
For such is the overthrow of an ungodly person, and from the earth it will cause another to sprout.
For the Lord will certainly not reject the innocent, but He will accept no gift of an ungodly person.
He will fill the mouth of true people with laughter, and their lips with thanksgiving.
Their enemies will be clothed with shame, and an ungodly person’s dwelling will be no more.”
After the Lord had spoken all these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You and your two friends sinned, for you spoke nothing true before Me, as My servant Job did.

Now take seven calves and seven rams and go to My servant Job, and he will make an offering on your behalf. My servant Job will pray for you, for I will surely accept his person. Were it not for him, I would have destroyed you; for you did not speak truth against My servant Job.”
Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Minaean went and did as the Lord commanded them, and He released their sin through Job.
The Lord increased Job. When he also prayed for his friends, He forgave their sin. The Lord gave double what Job had formerly, for a doubling.

All his brothers and sisters heard everything that had happened to him and came to him, along with all who had known him from the beginning. They ate and drank with him and consoled him, and marveled at all the Lord had brought upon him. Each gave him one ewe lamb and an unstamped gold piece of four drachmas.
The Lord blessed Job’s latter things more than the former. His livestock were fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen and one thousand grazing female donkeys.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
He called the first Hemera, the second Casia and the third Amalthea’s Horn.
None were found beneath heaven better than Job’s daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
After the affliction, Job lived one hundred seventy years; in all, he lived two hundred forty-eight years. Job saw his sons and his sons’ sons, a fourth generation.
Job died elderly and full of days.
Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit rejoiced in God my Savior,
because He looked upon the lowly condition of His servant. For behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is His name.
His mercy is for generations and generations upon those who fear Him.
He has performed a mighty deed with His arm; He scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.
He brought rulers down from thrones and raised up the lowly.
He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He helped Israel His servant, remembering mercy,
as He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring forever.”
He showed him the weight of the incense altar of tested gold, and the pattern of the chariot of the cherubim with outspread wings, overshadowing the ark of the Lord’s covenant.
David gave Solomon everything in writing from the Lord’s hand, according to the understanding that had come to him about carrying out the pattern.

David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong, be of good courage, and act. Do not fear or be dismayed, for the Lord my God is with you. He will not let you go nor forsake you, until you finish all the work of ministry in the Lord’s house.

Behold, the service courses of the priests and Levites are ready for all ministry in God’s house, and are with you in every undertaking, together with everyone eager and wise in every craft. The rulers and all the people are ready for all your words.”
I hated all my toil with which I toil beneath the sun, because I leave it to the person who comes after me.
Who knows whether he will be wise or foolish? Yet he has authority over all the toil with which I labored and acted wisely beneath the sun. This too is futility.
I turned to bid my heart farewell concerning all the toil with which I had labored beneath the sun,
for a person may toil with wisdom, knowledge and courage, yet will give his portion to someone who did not toil for it. This too is futility and a great evil.
For what comes to a person from all his toil and the resolve of his heart with which he toils beneath the sun?
For all his days are pain, and his distraction is anger; even at night his heart does not sleep. This too is futility.
There is no good in a person. What he will eat and drink and let his soul see as good in his toil—I saw that this too is from the hand of God.
For who will eat, and who will abstain, apart from Him?

For to the person who is good before Him He gave wisdom, knowledge and gladness; but to the sinner He gave the distraction of adding and gathering, to give to the one who is good before God. This too is futility and resolve of spirit.
And Jacob lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, Esau his brother was coming, and four hundred men with him. And Jacob divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two slave women.
And he put the two slave women and their sons first, and Leah and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
And he himself went before them, and bowed down to the earth seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him, and fell upon his neck; and they both wept.
And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children with whom God has shown mercy to your servant.”
And the slave women and their children drew near, and bowed down.
And Leah and her children drew near, and bowed down; and afterward Rachel and Joseph drew near, and bowed down.
And he said, “What do you mean by all these companies which I met?” And he said, “That your servant may find grace in your sight, my lord.”
And Esau said, “I have much, brother; let what is yours be yours.”
And Jacob said, “If I have found grace in your sight, receive the gifts from my hands; for I have seen your face as one might see the face of God, and you will accept me.
“Take my blessings which I have brought to you, for God has shown mercy to me, and I have all things.” And he urged him, and he took them.

And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and His ordinances which I command you this day, that it may be well with you?
Behold, unto the Lord your God belong heaven and the heaven of heaven, the earth and all that is therein.
Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and chose their seed after them, even you, above all the nations, as at this day.
And you shall circumcise your hardness of heart, and shall stiffen your neck no more.
For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.
And you shall love the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him, and you shall cleave unto Him, and you shall swear by His name.
He is your boast, and He is your God, who has done among you these great and glorious things which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy souls; but now the Lord your God has made you as the stars of heaven in multitude.
For heaven will be new and earth new, and they will never remember former things, nor will those things enter their heart,
but they will find joy and exultation in it. For behold, I am making Jerusalem an exultation and My people joy.
I will exult over Jerusalem and rejoice over My people, and no sound of weeping or crying will ever again be heard in her.

There will never be one cut off prematurely there, nor an old man who fails to complete his time. For the young person will be a hundred years old, but the sinner who dies will be a hundred years old and accursed.
They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
They will not build for others to inhabit or plant for others to eat. For My people’s days will be like those of the tree of life; they will wear out the works of their labor.
My chosen ones will not labor in vain or bear children for a curse, because they are offspring blessed by God, and their descendants will be with them.
Before they cry out I will listen to them; while they are still speaking I will say, ‘What is it?’
Then wolves and lambs will graze together, and a lion will eat straw like an ox, while a serpent will eat earth like bread. They will not wrong or destroy on My holy mountain,” says the Lord.
Your mother was like a vine, like a blossom on a pomegranate tree, planted by water; her fruit and her shoot came from abundant water.
She had a rod of strength for a tribe of leaders; it rose in her size among the trunks, and it saw her size among the multitude of her branches.
She was broken off in wrath and thrown to the ground. The scorching wind dried her choice parts; her rod of strength was punished and dried up. Fire consumed her.
Now they have planted her in the wilderness, in a waterless land,
and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”
And you, do not pray for this people or petition for them with supplication and prayer, because I will not listen when they call upon Me, in their time of affliction.
Why has the beloved woman committed an abomination in My house? Will prayers and holy meats remove your evils from you, or will you escape by these?
The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, well-shaded in appearance. At the sound of its pruning, fire was kindled upon it; great is the affliction upon you, and its branches became useless.
And the Lord who planted you spoke evils against you in return for the evil of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, because they acted for themselves to provoke Me by burning incense to Baal.
Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will greatly delight in His commandments.
His seed will be powerful in the land; a generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness remains for an age of an age.
Light sprang up in darkness for the upright— merciful, compassionate and righteous.
Kind is the man who has compassion and lends; he will manage his words with judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous person will be an everlasting memorial.
He will not fear an evil report; his heart is ready to hope in the Lord.
His heart is established; he shall certainly not fear, until he looks upon his enemies.
He scattered gifts; he gave to the poor. His righteousness remains for an age of an age; his horn will be raised in glory.
A sinner will see and be angry; he will gnash his teeth and waste away; the desire of sinners will perish.
The Lord said to me, From the north calamities will be kindled upon all who inhabit the land.

Because behold, I am summoning all the kingdoms from the north of the land, says the Lord. They will come and each set his throne at the forecourts of Jerusalem’s gates, against all her surrounding walls and against all Judah’s cities.
I will speak to them with judgment concerning all their evil, because they abandoned Me, sacrificed to foreign gods and bowed down to the works of their hands.
But you, gird your waist, rise and tell them everything I command you. Do not fear them or be terrified before them, because I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord.
Behold, on this day I have made you like a fortified city and like a strong bronze wall against all Judah’s kings, its rulers and the people of the land,
and they will fight you, but they will certainly not prevail against you, because I am with you to rescue you, said the Lord.
The Lord gives me a tongue of instruction, to know the right time when a word must be spoken. He appointed morning for me; He added an ear for me to hear,
and the Lord’s instruction opens my ears. I do not disobey or contradict.
I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.
The Lord became my helper; therefore I was not abashed. Instead, I set my face like solid rock and knew that I would certainly not be ashamed.
For the One who justified me draws near. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him stand against me together. Who is bringing a case against me? Let him approach me.
Behold, the Lord helps me. Who will harm me? Behold, all of you will grow old like a garment, and it will devour you like a moth.
Of David. Judge, Lord, those who wrong me; make war on those who make war on me.
Take hold of weapon and shield, and rise to my aid.
Draw the sword and close the way against those pursuing me; say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
Let those who seek my soul be ashamed and abashed; let those devising evils for me turn backward and be put to shame.
Let them become like dust before the wind, with an angel of the Lord pressing them out.
Let their way become darkness and a slippery path, with an angel of the Lord pursuing them.
For without cause they hid for me the destruction of their trap; without purpose they reproached my soul.
Let a trap they do not know come upon them; let the snare they hid catch them, and into that trap they will fall.
Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you did pray to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.
This is the word the Lord has spoken concerning him: Virgin daughter Zion despises you and sneers at you; daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice? You have lifted your eyes on high against Israel’s Holy One!

Through your messengers you did reproach the Lord and did say, “With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks. I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.
I cooled and drank foreign waters, and with my foot’s tread I dried up all rivers of enclosure.”
I formed it; now I brought it. It became a carrying away into exiles of fighting men—fortified cities.
Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed. They became field grass or green herbage, rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.
I know your sitting, your going out, your coming in, and your anger against Me.
Because you were angry with Me and your arrogance rose to My ears, I shall put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and turn you back by the road on which you came.
Naomi had an acquaintance of her husband, a man mighty in strength, of the kindred of Abimelech. His name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, “Let me go now into a field and glean among the ears of grain after someone in whose eyes I find favour.” She said to her, “Go, daughter.”
And she went and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and by chance she came upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the kindred of Abimelech.
And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “The Lord be with you.” They said to him, “May the Lord bless you.”
Boaz said to his servant who was in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?”
The servant in charge of the reapers answered, “She is the Moabite girl who returned with Naomi from the field of Moab,
and she said, ‘Let me glean now, and gather among the sheaves after the reapers.’ She came and stood from morning until evening; she did not rest in the field, even a little.”
He stood before the Lord’s altar, opposite all Israel’s assembly, and spread out his hands.

For Solomon had made a bronze base and put it in the middle of the temple court, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high. He stood on it, fell on his knees opposite all Israel’s assembly, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
He said, “Lord, Israel’s God, there is no god like Thee in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and mercy for Thy servants who walk before Thee with their whole heart.

For they will sin against Thee—for there will be no human being who will not sin—and Thou wilt strike them and hand them over before enemies, and their captors will carry them captive to an enemy land, a land far away or near,
and they turn their heart in their land where they were deported, and indeed return and supplicate Thee in their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, done wrong, and acted lawlessly,’

and return to Thee with all their heart and all their soul in the land of those who took them captive, and pray toward their land that Thou didst give their fathers, the city Thou didst choose, and the house I built for Thy name,
then hear from heaven, from Thy prepared dwelling place, their prayer and supplication, execute judgments, and be propitious toward the people who sinned against Thee.
Now, O Lord, I beseech Thee, let Thine eyes be open, and Thine ears attentive to the supplication of this place.
Now arise, O Lord God, to Thy rest, Thou and the ark of Thy strength. Let Thy priests, O Lord God, clothe themselves with salvation, and let Thy sons rejoice in good things.
Lord God, do not turn away the face of Thine anointed one. Remember the mercies of David Thy servant.”
What can we say, our God, after this? For we have abandoned Thy commandments,

which Thou gavest us through Thy servants the prophets, saying, ‘The land you are entering to inherit is a land being moved amid the movement of the peoples of the nations, in their repulsive practices, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleanness.

Now do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take some of their daughters for your sons. You shall never seek their peace or good, so that you may become strong, eat the good things of the land and bequeath it to your sons for ever.’
After everything that has come upon us through our evil deeds and our great offense—for there is none like our God, because Thou hast lightened our lawless deeds and given us deliverance—
for we have returned to scattering Thy commandments and intermarrying with the peoples of the lands. Do not be provoked against us to the point of destruction, so that no remnant or survivor remains.
Lord, God of Israel, Thou art righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as on this day. Here we are before Thee in our offenses, for because of this there is no standing before Thee.”
I set my face toward the Lord God to find prayer and mercy, with fasts, sackcloth, and ashes.
I prayed to the Lord God and confessed, saying, “Behold, Lord, Thou art the great, strong, and fearsome God, keeping the covenant and mercy for those who love Thee and guard Thy commands:
we have sinned, done wrong, acted impiously, fallen away, and transgressed Thy commandments and judgments,
and have not listened to Thy servants the prophets, to what they spoke in Thy name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and every nation upon the earth.

Righteousness belongs to Thee, Lord, but shame of face to us as on this day—to the people of Judah, those dwelling in Jerusalem, and all the people Israel, near and far, in all the countries where Thou didst scatter them because of the trespass they committed before Thee.
Master, shame of face belongs to us, to our kings, rulers, and fathers, because we have sinned against Thee.
To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy, for we have fallen away from Thee
and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow Thy law that Thou didst set before Moses and us through Thy servants the prophets.
Eleven: Chaph. My soul fails with longing for Thy salvation, and I placed my hope in Thy word.
My eyes failed with longing for Thy saying, saying, “When wilt Thou comfort me?”
For I became like a wineskin in frost; I did not forget Thine ordinances.
How many are the days of Thy servant? When wilt Thou give me judgment against those who pursue me?
Lawbreakers told me idle tales, but not in keeping with Thy law, Lord.
All Thy commandments are truth; they pursued me unjustly—help me.
They nearly brought me to an end on the earth, but I did not forsake Thy commandments.
Give me life according to Thy mercy, and I will keep the testimonies of Thy mouth.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
just as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, so that we should be holy and without blemish before Him in love,
having predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to Himself, according to the good pleasure of His will,
to the praise of the glory of His grace, with which He favored us in the Beloved.
In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of transgressions, according to the riches of His grace,
which He lavished on us in all wisdom and understanding,
having made known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure which He purposed in Him,
for an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth, in Him.
For thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I turn toward them like a river of peace, and like a flooding torrent the glory of nations. Their children will be lifted on shoulders and comforted on knees.
As if a mother were to comfort someone, so I too will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you will be comforted.’
You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will spring up like vegetation. The Lord’s hand will be known to those who revere Him, and He will threaten the disobedient.
He called Solomon his son and commanded him to build the house for the Lord, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, “Child, it came upon my soul to build a house for the name of the Lord God.

But the Lord’s word came upon me, saying, ‘You have poured out much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for My name, because you have poured out much blood upon the earth before Me.

Behold, a son is born unto you; he shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all the enemies round about him, for Solomon is his name; and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.
He will build a house for My name. He will be a son to Me, and I will be a Father to him. I will set upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel for ever.’
Now, my son, the Lord will be with you, and He will grant success, and you will build a house for the Lord your God, as He spoke concerning you.
Only may the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, to observe and to do the law of the Lord your God.
Then He will grant success, if you take care to do the ordinances and judgments that the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel. Act courageously and be strong; do not fear or be terrified.
When the king was settled in his house and the Lord had given him possession on every side, away from all his surrounding enemies,
the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”
That night a word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
“Go and say to My servant David, ‘Thus says the Lord: You will not build Me a house for Me to dwell in,
for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day. I have been moving about in a lodging and a tent.
Wherever I passed through among all Israel, did I ever speak to one of Israel’s tribes whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, “Why have you not built Me a cedar house?”
Now say this to My servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be ruler over My people, over Israel,
and I was with you wherever you went and destroyed all your enemies before you, and I made you renowned, according to the name of the great ones on the earth.
I will appoint a place for My people Israel and plant them there. They will dwell on their own and worry no more. No unjust man will again humble them as at the beginning,
from the days when I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will announce to you that you will build Him a house.
When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will be from your own body, and prepare his kingdom.
He will build Me a house for My name, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. If his wrongdoing comes, I will correct him with the rod of men and the afflictions of human beings.
But I will not withdraw My mercy from him as I withdrew it from those whom I removed from before Me.
His house and his kingdom will be made sure for ever before Me, and his throne will be set upright for ever.’”
Nathan spoke to David according to all these words and all this vision.
He made houses for himself in the City of David, prepared the place for God’s ark, and made a tent for it.
Then David said, “No one may lift God’s ark except the Levites, for the Lord chose them to lift the Lord’s ark and to minister to Him for ever.”
David assembled all Israel in Jerusalem to bring the Lord’s ark up to the place he had prepared for it.

The men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up the ark of the Lord’s covenant. They brought it into Aminadab’s house on the hill and consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the Lord’s covenant.
From the day the ark was in Kiriath-jearim, the days multiplied until twenty years had passed. All Israel’s house looked after the Lord.
A psalm of David. The Lord has become King! Let peoples be angry. He sits upon the cherubim; let the earth be shaken.
The Lord is great in Zion and exalted above all the peoples.
Let them give thanks to Thy great name, for it is fearsome and holy.
The King’s honor loves judgment. Thou didst prepare uprightness; judgment and righteousness in Jacob Thou hast done.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at His footstool, for He is holy.
Moses and Aaron were among His priests, and Samuel among those who call on His name. They called upon the Lord, and He heard them,
He spoke to them in a pillar of cloud. They kept His testimonies and the ordinances He gave them.
Lord our God, Thou heardest them; God, Thou wast gracious to them and tookest vengeance for all their practices.
Exalt the Lord our God and bow down toward His holy mountain, for holy is the Lord our God.
Peter stood with the eleven, raised his voice, and addressed them: “Men of Judea and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and listen closely to my words.
These people are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.
Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
For David says concerning Him, ‘I kept the Lord before me always, for He is at my right hand so that I will not be shaken.
Therefore my heart rejoiced and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh will dwell in hope,
because Thou wilt not abandon my soul to Hades, nor allow Thy Holy One to see decay.
Thou hast made known to me the paths of life; Thou wilt fill me with gladness in Thy presence.’
Men, brothers, I may speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
Since he was a prophet and knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
he foresaw and spoke about the resurrection of the Christ: He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see decay.
God raised this Jesus, and all of us are witnesses of it.
Therefore, exalted to God’s right hand and having received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit, He has poured out what you both see and hear.
For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand
until I make Thy enemies a footstool for Thy feet.”’
Therefore let the whole house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified.”
Solomon stood before the Lord’s altar in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel and spread his hands toward heaven.
He said, “Lord, the God of Israel, there is no God like Thee in heaven above or on earth beneath, keeping covenant and mercy with Thy servant who walks before Thee with all his heart,
which Thou keptest for Thy servant David my father; Thou spakest with Thy mouth and didst fulfill it with Thy hands, as it is this day.

Now, Lord, the God of Israel, keep for Thy servant David my father what Thou didst promise him: ‘A man of yours shall not be removed from before Me sitting on Israel’s throne, if only your children guard their ways, walking before Me as you have walked before Me.’
Now, Lord, the God of Israel, let Thy word to David my father indeed be confirmed.
But will God truly dwell with people on earth? If heaven and the heaven of heaven are not sufficient for Thee, how much less this house that I have built for Thy name!
Look upon my supplication, Lord, the God of Israel, to hear the rejoicing that Thy servant offers in prayer before Thee, to Thee, this day,
so that Thine eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which Thou saidst, ‘My name shall be there,’ to hear the prayer Thy servant prays toward this place day and night.
Hear the supplication of Thy servant and Thy people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear in Thy dwelling place, in heaven; act and be merciful.
And the Lord awoke like one sleeping, like a powerful man heavy with wine,
and struck His enemies backward; He gave them everlasting reproach.
And He rejected Joseph’s dwelling, and did not choose Ephraim’s tribe.
And He chose Judah’s tribe, Mount Zion, which He loved,
and built His sanctuary like that of one-horned beasts; in the earth He founded it for ever.
And He chose David His servant, and took him up from the flocks of sheep;
from behind the ewes giving birth He took him, to shepherd Jacob His people and Israel His inheritance.
And he shepherded them in his heart’s innocence, and guided them with his hands’ understanding.
A mountain of God, a rich mountain; a curdled mountain, a rich mountain.
Why do you suppose, curdled mountains, that this is the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell? For indeed the Lord will dwell to the end.
God’s chariot is ten-thousandfold, thousands of flourishing ones; the Lord is among them, in Sinai, in the holy place.
Thou didst ascend on high; Thou tookest captivity captive; Thou didst receive gifts among humankind, and indeed the disobedient, to establish a dwelling. Blessed is the Lord God.
because He did not despise or resent the poor man’s petition, nor turn His face away from me, and when I cried out to Him, He heard me.
From Thee comes my praise in a great assembly; I will repay my vows before those who fear Him.
The needy will eat and be filled, and those who seek the Lord will praise Him; their hearts will live for the age of the age.
All the limits of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Thee,
because kingship belongs to the Lord, and He is master of the nations.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and accomplished redemption for His people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant,
as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from long ago:
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant,
the oath He swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, rescued from our enemies’ hand, we might serve Him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
And you also, child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare His ways,
to give His people knowledge of salvation in the forgiveness of their sins,
through the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,
to shine upon those who sit in darkness and death’s shadow, to direct our feet into a way of peace.”

At that time Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road and took him aside from the road. Ahijah was clothed in a new garment, and both were in the plain.
Ahijah took hold of his new garment which he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
He said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, because thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘Behold, I am tearing the kingdom from Solomon’s hand and will give you ten scepters.
But two scepters shall remain his, because of My servant David and because of Jerusalem, the city I chose from all Israel’s tribes,

because he abandoned Me and made provision for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh and Moab’s idols, and for their king, the offense of the sons of Ammon. He did not walk in My ways to do what is right before Me as David his father did.
Yet I will certainly not take the whole kingdom from his hand, because I will surely oppose him all the days of his life, because of David My servant, whom I chose.
