I will take the kingdom from his son’s hand and give you the ten scepters.
I will give his son the two scepters, so that My servant David may have a place before Me always in Jerusalem, the city I chose for Myself to place My name there.
I will take you, and you shall reign over what your soul desires; you shall be king over Israel.

If you keep all I command you, walk in My ways, and do what is right before Me, keeping My commandments and ordinances as David My servant did, then I will be with you and build you a faithful house as I built for David.’”
Help me, Lord my God; save me according to Thy mercy,
and let them know that this is Thy hand and that Thou, Lord, hast done it.
They will curse, but Thou wilt bless; let those rising against me be ashamed, but Thy servant will rejoice.
Let those slandering me wear humiliation and wrap themselves in their shame like a double cloak.
I will greatly thank the Lord with my mouth and praise Him among many,
for He stood at a poor person’s right hand, to save from those pursuing my soul.
So those who welcomed his word were baptized, and about three thousand persons were added that day.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.
Awe came upon everyone, and many wonders and signs took place through the apostles.
All who believed were together and held everything in common.
They would sell their properties and possessions and distribute the proceeds to all, as anyone had need.
Day by day they devoted themselves with one accord to gathering in the temple, and breaking bread in their homes, they shared food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
praising God and enjoying favor with all the people. And day by day the Lord added those who were being saved to their gathering.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Take Aaron and his sons, his robes, the anointing oil, the calf for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
And assemble the whole congregation at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses did as the Lord directed him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the Tent of Testimony.
And Moses said unto the congregation: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

And he clothed him with the tunic, girded him with the belt, clothed him with the under-robe, and put the shoulder-piece on him. He girded him according to the shoulder-piece’s workmanship and fastened him securely in it.
And he placed the oracle-piece on it and put Manifestation and Truth upon the oracle-piece.
And he put the turban on his head and placed on its front the gold plate, the consecrated holy object, as the Lord directed Moses.
And Moses took some of the anointing oil,

and sprinkled some of it on the altar seven times. He anointed the altar and consecrated it, and all its utensils, the basin and its stand, and consecrated them. He anointed the tent and everything in it and consecrated it.
And Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them with tunics, girded them with belts, and put turbans on them, as the Lord directed Moses.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you grew weak in your injustices.
Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Speak to Him so that you do not receive injustice but receive good things, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.
Assur will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse, and we will certainly no longer call the works of our hands “Our gods.” The One in you will have mercy on an orphan.
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and settle beneath his shelter; they will live and be filled to intoxication with grain. His memorial will blossom like a vine, like Lebanon’s wine.
As for Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a thickly shading juniper; from Me your fruit is found.
Who is wise and will understand these things, or discerning and will recognize them? For the Lord’s ways are straight; the righteous will walk in them, but the impious will grow weak in them.
A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judea.
God, my God, toward Thee I rise at dawn; my soul thirsted for Thee. How greatly my flesh longs for Thee in a desert, trackless and waterless land!
So I was seen by Thee in the holy place, to see Thy power and Thy glory.
For Thy mercy is better than lives; my lips will praise Thee.
So I will bless Thee in my life; in Thy name I will lift my hands.
May my soul be filled as with fat and richness, and my mouth will praise with lips of exultation.
If I remembered Thee upon my bed, in the dawn hours I meditated upon Thee.
For Thou becamest my helper, and in the shelter of Thy wings I will exult.
My soul clung behind Thee; Thy right hand supported me.
But they sought my soul in vain; they will enter the lowest places of the earth.
They will be handed over into the hands of a sword; they will be portions for foxes.
But the king will rejoice in God; everyone swearing by Him will be praised, for the mouth of those speaking unjust things was stopped.
Hallelujah! Praise the Lord, servants; praise the name of the Lord.
May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and for ever.
From the sun’s risings to its settings, praise the name of the Lord.
The Lord is high above all nations; His glory is above the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God, who dwells in high places,
and looks upon lowly things in heaven and on earth?
He raises the poor from the ground and lifts the needy from the dung heap,
to seat him with rulers, with the rulers of His people.
He settles a barren woman in a house as a mother of children rejoicing.
Hallelujah. Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; may praise be pleasing to our God.
The Lord builds Jerusalem, and He will gather the dispersed of Israel.
He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their fractures.
He numbers multitudes of stars and calls them all by names.
Great is our Lord, and great is His strength; His understanding is beyond number.
The Lord takes up the meek, but brings sinners low to the ground.
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, above all the nations upon the face of the earth.
The Lord preferred you and chose you, not because you were more numerous than all the nations, for you are the fewest of all the nations,

but because the Lord loved you, and kept the oath which He sware unto your fathers, the Lord brought you forth with a mighty hand and with an uplifted arm, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, out of the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments, unto a thousand generations,
and repays them that hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He shall not delay with them that hate Him; He shall repay them to their face.
And you shall keep these commandments, and ordinances, and judgments, which I command you this day to do.

Moses told his father-in-law everything the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the hardship they had met on the journey, and how the Lord had delivered them from Pharaoh’s hand and the Egyptians’ hand.
Jethro was amazed at all the good the Lord had done for them in delivering them from the Egyptians’ hand and Pharaoh’s hand.
Jethro said, “Blessed be the Lord, for He delivered His people from the Egyptians’ hand and Pharaoh’s hand.
Now I know that the Lord is greater than all gods, because of this, because they attacked them.”
Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for God. Aaron and all Israel’s elders came to eat bread with Moses’ father-in-law before God.
Hallelujah. At Israel’s departure from Egypt, the house of Jacob from a foreign-speaking people,
Judea became His sanctuary, Israel His authority.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned backward.
The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs of sheep.
What is it with you, sea, that you fled, and with you, Jordan, that you withdrew backward?
Mountains, that you skipped like rams, and hills, like lambs of sheep?
Before the Lord the earth was shaken, before the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into pools of water and the sheer rock into springs of water.
Not to us, Lord, not to us, but only to Thy name give glory, because of Thy mercy and Thy truth,
lest the nations say, “Where is their God?”
But our God is in heaven above; in the heavens and on the earth He has done everything He wished.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, works of human hands.
They have a mouth and will not speak; they have eyes and will not see.
They have ears and will not hear; they have noses and will not smell.
They have hands and will not feel; feet, and will not walk; they will not sound with their throat.
May those who make them become like them, and all who have put their trust in them.
The house of Israel hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
The house of Aaron hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
Those who fear the Lord hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
The Lord remembered us and blessed us; He blessed the house of Israel; He blessed the house of Aaron.
He blessed those who fear the Lord, the small together with the great.
May the Lord add to you, to you and to your sons.
You are blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
The heaven of heaven belongs to the Lord, but the earth He gave to the sons of men.
The dead will not praise Thee, Lord, nor any who descend into Hades,
but we, the living, will bless the Lord from now and for ever.
Hear the Lord’s word that He spoke concerning you, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the nations’ ways, and do not fear heaven’s signs, because they fear them before their faces.
For the nations’ customs are futile: it is wood cut from the woodland, a carpenter’s work and a cast object.
They are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they fastened them, and they will not move.
They must be lifted and carried, because they will not take a step. Do not fear them, because they certainly will not do evil, and no good is in them.
It is worked silver; they will not walk. Applied silver will come from Tarshish, gold from Mophaz, and the goldsmiths’ hand; all are artisans’ works. They will dress them in blue and purple.
This is what you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
The Lord who made the earth by His strength, who set the inhabited world upright by His wisdom, also stretched out heaven by His understanding,
and an abundance of water in heaven; and He brought clouds up from the earth’s extremity, made lightning for rain, and brought light out of His treasuries.
Every human became foolish, without knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame at his carved things, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them.
They are futile, mocked works; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob’s portion is not such as this, because the One who formed everything is himself his inheritance; Lord is His name.

At midnight the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on the throne to the firstborn of the captive woman in the pit, and the firstborn of every animal of the livestock.
Pharaoh rose during the night, with all his attendants and all the Egyptians. There was a great cry throughout the land of Egypt, for there was no house without someone dead.
And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron by night, and said to them, “Rise and depart from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; go, serve the Lord your God, as you say.
Take your sheep and your cattle, and go. Bless me also.”
The Egyptians pressed the people hard to drive them quickly out of the land, for they said, “We are all dying!”
The people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneaded batches wrapped in their garments on their shoulders.
The sons of Israel did as Moses had instructed them. They asked the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold and for clothing.
The Lord gave His people favour in the Egyptians’ sight, and they lent to them. Thus they plundered the Egyptians.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, I have made you a god to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
You shall speak to him all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he may let the sons of Israel go out of his land.
I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh will not listen to you. I will lay My hand on Egypt and bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with My power and great vengeance.
All the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when I stretch out My hand over Egypt and bring the sons of Israel out from among them.”
Moses and Aaron did as the Lord commanded them; so they did.
Moses was eighty years old and his brother Aaron eighty-three when he spoke to Pharaoh.

These are the kings of the land whom the sons of Israel killed, whose land they inherited beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the Arnon ravine to Mount Hermon and all the land of Arabah eastward:
Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which is in the ravine, along part of the ravine, and half of Gilead as far as Jabbok, the borders of the sons of Ammon,
and Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth toward the east, and as far as the Sea of Arabah, the Salt Sea on the east, by the road toward Asimoth, from Thaiman beneath Asedoth Phasga;
and Og king of Bashan, one of the remaining giants, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei,
ruling from Mount Hermon and Salcah over all Bashan as far as the borders of Geshur and Maacah, and half of Gilead, the borders of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the Lord and the sons of Israel struck them, and Moses gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the Amorites whom Joshua and the sons of Israel killed beyond the Jordan toward the sea, at Baal-gad in the plain of Lebanon and as far as Mount Chelcha on the ascent to Seir. Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel to inherit according to their lot,
in the mountain, the plain, Arabah, Asedoth, the wilderness, and the Negeb: the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite:
the king of Jericho and the king of Ai, which is near Bethel;
the king of Jerusalem; the king of Hebron;
the king of Jarmuth; the king of Lachish;
the king of Ailam; the king of Gezer;

Ask now of the former days that were before you, from the day when God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven unto the other: has there been anything like this great matter, or has such a thing been heard?
Has a nation heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Or has God attempted to go and take unto Himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trial, and by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an uplifted arm, and by great visions, according to all that the Lord our God did in Egypt before your eyes?
That you might know that the Lord your God, He is God, and there is none beside Him.
Out of heaven His voice was made heard, to instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, even you, and Himself brought you forth out of Egypt by His great strength,
to destroy nations great and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, and to give you their land to inherit, as you have this day.
And you shall know this day, and lay it to mind, that the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and upon earth beneath; there is none beside Him.

And you shall keep His ordinances and His commandments which I command you this day, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for ever.
And Moses said to God, “Behold, I shall go to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you’; and they shall ask me, ‘What is His name?’ What shall I say to them?”
And God said to Moses, “I am the One Who Is.” And He said, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘The One Who Is has sent me to you.’”

And God said again to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is My everlasting name, and My memorial from generation to generation.

Go, therefore, gather the council of elders of the sons of Israel, and say to them, ‘The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying, “I have surely visited you, and seen all that has befallen you in Egypt.

And I have said, I will bring you up out of the affliction of the Egyptians, into the land of the Canaanites, and Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Girgashites, and Hivites, and Jebusites, into a land flowing with milk and honey.”’
Behold, are not these things gathered with Me, and sealed in My treasuries?
In the day of vengeance I will repay, in the season when their foot shall slip; for the day of their destruction is near, and the things prepared for you are at hand.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they trusted,
whose sacrifices’ fat you ate, and whose drink offerings’ wine you drank? Let them arise and help you, and become your protectors.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.
For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.

These were Levi’s sons according to their ancestral houses, their ancestral rulers according to their inspection, by the number of their names, head by head, doing the works of ministry in the Lord’s house, from twenty years old and upward.
For David said, “The Lord, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has dwelt in Jerusalem for ever.”
The Levites were no longer carrying the tent and all its vessels for its ministry.
For David’s last words record the number of Levi’s sons from twenty years old and upward,
for he stationed them at Aaron’s hand to minister in the Lord’s house, over the courts and chambers, over the purification of all holy things, and over the works of ministry in God’s house:
for the bread of presentation, the fine flour of the sacrifice, the unleavened flat cakes, the pan preparation, the mixed preparation, and every measure;
and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks unto the Lord, and likewise in the evening;
and over all the whole burnt offerings offered to the Lord on sabbaths, new moons, and feasts, by number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually for the Lord.
They shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony and the charges of Aaron’s sons their brethren, to minister in the Lord’s house.
Give unto the Lord the glory of His name; take gifts and bring them before Him, and bow before the Lord in His holy courts.
Let all the earth fear before Him; let the earth be set right and not be shaken.
Let heaven be glad and the earth exult; let them say among the nations, “The Lord reigns!”
The sea shall resound with its fullness, and the tree of the field and everything in it.
Then the trees of the forest shall be glad before the Lord, for He has come to judge the earth.
Give thanks unto the Lord, for it is good, for His mercy endures for ever.
Say, “Save us, O God of our salvation, and rescue us from the nations, that we may praise Thy holy name and glory in Thy praises.”
Blessed be the Lord, Israel’s God, from age to age! All the people shall say, “Amen.” And they praised the Lord.
But you, O man of God, flee these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.
Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of eternal life, to which you were called. And you confessed the good confession before many witnesses.
I command you before God, who preserves all things alive, and Christ Jesus, who testified the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
that you keep the commandment spotless, above reproach, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which the blessed and only Sovereign will display at the proper times, the King of those who reign and Lord of those who rule,
who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no human being has seen or can see; to Him be honor and eternal might. Amen.
Let his name be blessed through the ages; before the sun his name will endure. And all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him; all nations will call him blessed.
Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders!
And blessed be His glorious name for the age and for the age of the age; and the whole earth will be filled with His glory. May it be! May it be!
A psalm of David, for the first day of the week. The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord, the inhabited world and all who dwell in it.
He founded it upon seas and prepared it upon rivers.
Who will ascend the Lord’s mountain, and who will stand in His holy place?
One innocent in hands and pure in heart, who did not take up his soul for emptiness and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.
This one will receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.
This is the generation of those who seek Him, who seek the face of Jacob’s God. Diapsalma.
And God said, “Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth and to divide the day from the night. Let them serve for signs and seasons, for days and years.
And let them be lights in the firmament of heaven, to shine upon the earth.” And it was so.
And God made the two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; He made the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth,
to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening, and there was morning: a fourth day.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Consecrate to Me every firstborn, the first offspring opening every womb among the sons of Israel, both human and animal. It is Mine.”

And Moses said to the people, “Remember this day, in which you came out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from here; and no leaven shall be eaten.
For today you go out, in the month of new grain.

And when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites, and Hittites, and Hivites, and Girgashites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall keep this service in this month.
You shall eat unleavened bread for six days, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast of the Lord.
For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; no leavened thing shall be seen with you, neither shall there be leaven with you within all your borders.
And you shall declare to your son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of this that the Lord God acted for me when I came out of Egypt.’
And it shall be to you a sign upon your hand, and a memorial before your eyes, that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt.
You shall keep this law at the appointed times of the seasons, from year to year.
The angel of God, who went before the camp of the sons of Israel, moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from before them and stood behind them.
It came between the Egyptians’ camp and Israel’s camp and stood there. There were darkness and gloom, and the night passed. They did not mingle with one another all night.
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The Lord drove the sea back with a violent south wind all night and made the sea dry. The water was split.
The sons of Israel entered the midst of the sea on dry ground, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh’s horses, the chariots, and the riders entered after them into the midst of the sea.
During the morning watch, the Lord looked on the Egyptians’ camp in a pillar of fire and cloud and threw the Egyptians’ camp into confusion.
He bound the axles of their chariots and drove them with force. The Egyptians said, “Let us flee from Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water return and cover the Egyptians, both their chariots and their riders.”
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and toward daybreak the water returned to its place. The Egyptians fled beneath the water, and the Lord shook the Egyptians into the midst of the sea.
The water returned and covered the chariots, the riders, and all Pharaoh’s force that had entered the sea after them. Not one of them remained.
But the sons of Israel walked on dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
The Lord rescued Israel that day from the Egyptians’ hand, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
Israel saw the great hand in what the Lord had done to the Egyptians. The people feared the Lord and trusted God and His attendant Moses.
Take heed unto yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, and fail to keep His commandments, and His judgments, and His ordinances which I command you this day;
lest, when you have eaten and are filled, and have built good houses and dwelt in them,
and your herds and your flocks are multiplied, and your silver and your gold are multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied,
you become lifted up in heart, and forget the Lord your God, who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage;

who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, wherein were biting serpents, and scorpions, and thirst, where there was no water; who brought forth for you a spring of water out of the sheer rock;
who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, to afflict you and to test you, and to do you good in your latter days.
Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.
And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.

And it shall be, if you utterly forget the Lord your God, and go after other gods, and serve them, and bow down unto them, I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall surely perish.
As the other nations which the Lord destroys from before you, so shall you perish, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
And Moses sent envoys to Sihon king of the Amorites with words of peace, saying:

We will pass through your land; we will travel by the road. We will not turn aside into fields or vineyards or drink water from your well. We will travel the royal road until we have passed through your territory.

And Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. He gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness to array himself against Israel. He came to Jahaz and arrayed himself against Israel.
And Israel struck him by slaughter with the sword, and they took control of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the sons of Ammon, because Jazer is the border of the sons of Ammon.
And Israel took all these towns and settled in all the Amorite towns, in Heshbon and all the towns adjoining it.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had previously fought the king of Moab, and they took all his land from Aroer as far as the Arnon.
Therefore those who speak in riddles will say: Come to Heshbon, so that Sihon's city may be built and prepared.
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city. It consumed as far as Moab and swallowed the pillars of the Arnon.
Woe unto you, Moab! You are ruined, people of Chemosh. Their sons were handed over to escape, and their daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites.
And their seed shall perish, from Heshbon as far as Dibon; and the women kindled still more fire against Moab.
Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites.
And Moses sent men to inspect Jazer. They captured it and its villages and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
And they turned and went up by the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out to meet them with all his people, for battle at Edrei.

And the Lord said unto Moses: Do not fear him, for I have handed him, all his people, and all his land into your hands. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.
And he struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until he left none of his alive; and they inherited their land.
And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the rulers of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel.

And Moses said to them: If the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad cross the Jordan with you, everyone equipped for war before the Lord, and you gain dominion over the land before you, you shall give them the land of Gilead as a possession.

But if they do not cross over equipped with you for war before the Lord, you shall bring their dependents, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they shall receive an inheritance among you in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Reuben and sons of Gad answered: Everything our lord says unto his servants, we will do.
We will cross over equipped before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you shall give us our possession on this side of the Jordan.

And Moses gave to the sons of Gad, the sons of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of the sons of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land and its towns with its boundaries, the towns of the surrounding land.
After those many days the king of Egypt died. The sons of Israel groaned deeply because of their labour and cried out, and their cry because of their labour rose to God.
God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
God looked upon the sons of Israel, and He became known to them.
Hallelujah. Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good; His mercy is for ever.
Let those redeemed by the Lord say so, those He redeemed from the enemy’s hand.
He gathered them from the countries, from east and west and north and the sea.
Thy kingdom is a kingdom of all ages, and Thy lordship endures through every generation.
Faithful is the Lord in His words, and holy in all His works.
The Lord supports all who are falling and raises up all who have been broken down.
The eyes of all hope in Thee, and Thou givest their food at the right time.
Thou openest Thy hand and fillest every living creature with good pleasure.
The Lord is righteous in all His ways and holy in all His works.
The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.
The Lord guards all who love Him, and all sinners He will utterly destroy.
My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise, and let all flesh bless His holy name for the age and for the age of the age.
The Song of Songs, which belongs to Solomon.
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are better than wine.
The fragrance of your perfumes surpasses all spices; your name is perfume poured out. That is why young women loved you.

They drew you; we will run after you into the fragrance of your perfumes. The king brought me into his chamber. Let us exult and rejoice in you; we will love your breasts more than wine. Uprightness loved you.
I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the tent coverings of Solomon.
Do not look at me because I have been darkened, because the sun looked upon me. My mother’s sons fought against me; they made me a keeper in vineyards. My own vineyard I did not keep.
Tell me, you whom my soul loved, where you pasture, where you rest at noon, lest I become like a woman covering herself beside your companions’ herds.
If you do not know yourself, beautiful among women, go out along the heels of the flocks and pasture your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
Our help is in the Lord’s name, who made heaven and earth.
A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.
A song of the ascents. Many times they fought against me from my youth— let Israel now say—
My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.
Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.
The Lord will bless you from Zion, who made heaven and earth.
A song of the ascents. Had the Lord not been among us— let Israel now say—
Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and for ever.
My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.
Thy priests will clothe themselves in righteousness, and Thy holy ones will exult.
you who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of our God’s house.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see Jerusalem’s good things all the days of your life.
For the Lord chose Zion; He selected her as His dwelling:
“This is My rest for age upon age; here I will dwell, for I selected her.
He struck many nations and killed powerful kings,
He gave their land as an inheritance, an inheritance to Israel His people.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords; for His mercy is for ever.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people,
training us so that, denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live self-controlled, just, and godly lives in the present age,
awaiting the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,
who gave Himself for us, so that He might ransom us from all lawlessness and purify for Himself a people for His own possession, eager for good works.
Speak these things, encourage, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
The one who does not love has not come to know God, because God is love.
In this the love of God was manifested among us: God has sent His only Son into the world so that we might live through Him.
In this is love: not that we have loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as propitiation for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
No one has ever beheld God. If we love one another, God abides in us, and His love has been brought to completion in us.
A psalm of a song, for the Sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord and make music to Thy name, Most High,
to declare Thy mercy in the morning and Thy truth by night,
on a ten-stringed psaltery, with song on a lyre.
“And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,
and say: What was your mother? A cub! She came to be among lions; among lions she multiplied her cubs.
One of her cubs sprang away; he became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
Nations heard against him; he was caught in their destruction, and they led him with a muzzle to Egypt’s land.
She saw that he had been driven away from her and that her support had perished; she took another of her cubs and appointed him a lion.
He moved among lions, became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.
He fed in his boldness, desolated their cities, and destroyed the land and its fullness by the sound of his roaring.
Nations from the surrounding countries set themselves against him and spread their nets over him; he was caught in their destruction.
They put him in a muzzle and a cage. He came to Babylon’s king, and he brought him into prison, so that his voice would not be heard upon Israel’s mountains.
For the end. A psalm of David, a song. Of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, from the account of the sojourn, when they were about to depart.
A hymn befits Thee, God, in Zion, and unto Thee a vow will be paid in Jerusalem.
Hear my prayer; unto Thee all flesh will come.
Words of lawless deeds overpowered us, and Thou wilt make atonement for our impieties.
Blessed is the one Thou didst choose and take to Thyself; he will dwell in Thy courts. We will be filled with the good things of Thy house; holy is Thy sanctuary, wondrous in righteousness.
Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness; let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first, for we became very poor.
Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,
lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants be known among the nations before our eyes.
Jehoshaphat fell asleep with his fathers and was buried beside his fathers in David’s city. His son Joram reigned in his place.
He had six brethren, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azarias, Iiel, Zacharias, Azarias, Michael, and Saphatias. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Their father gave them many gifts: silver, gold, and weapons, along with walled cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Joram, because he was the firstborn.
Joram rose over his kingdom and grew strong. He killed all his brethren with the sword, and some of Israel’s rulers.
When Joram was thirty-two years old, he was established over his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of Israel’s kings, as Ahab’s house had done, because Ahab’s daughter was his wife. He did what was evil before the Lord.
Yet the Lord was unwilling to destroy David’s house because of the covenant He had made with David, and as He had told him, to give him and his sons a lamp always.
David and his men went up and attacked all the Gesiri and the Amalekite. Behold, the land—from Gelampsour as far as the land of Egypt—was inhabited with suitable fortified settlements.
Yet the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah because of David His slave, as He had said He would give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.

Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the foreigner, and killed him. Then David’s men swore, “You must no longer go out with us to battle, and you must certainly not extinguish Israel’s lamp.”

target_units.text: Each spoke empty things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and a heart.

source_unit.text: Alas for me, for my sojourn has been prolonged; I have encamped among the tents of Kedar.

target_units.text: I am black and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the tent coverings of Solomon.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker was peaceable with people who hated peace and fought him without cause. Romans instructs its readers to live peaceably if possible and as far as it depends on them and to answer an enemy's need with good. The comparison joins peaceful conduct with continued hostility, preserving report and instruction as different forms.

source_unit.text: With those who hate peace I was peaceable; whenever I spoke to them, they fought me without cause.

target_units.text: If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.

But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker lifts his eyes to mountains and asks where help will come from; the next unit answers that help is from the Lord. Jeremiah calls the hills and mountains' power false and locates Israel's salvation in the Lord. The relation of mountains to divine help is compared without accusing the psalmist of worshiping mountains.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. I lifted my eyes to the mountains. From where will my help come?

target_units.text: Truly the hills and the power of the mountains were false; but through the Lord our God is Israel’s salvation.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Help from the maker of heaven and earth
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both identify the source of help with the Lord who made heaven and earth. Psalm 120 says help is from the Lord, while Psalm 123 locates help in His name; the distinctive creator-and-help formula is shared.

source_unit.text: My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

target_units.text: Our help is in the Lord’s name, who made heaven and earth.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source says not to give the foot over to shaking and wishes that the Keeper not slumber. Psalm 65 credits God with not giving the speaker's feet over to shaking. The foot-and-shaking expression corresponds; the sleep clause is additional to the source.

source_unit.text: Do not give your foot over to shaking, and may your Keeper not slumber.

target_units.text: He who set my soul in life and did not give my feet over to shaking.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The contrast with a sleeping deity
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm denies both slumber and sleep of Israel's guardian. Elijah's mockery suggests that Baal might be asleep. The particular contrast concerns a deity's sleeping, with Elijah's words retained as mockery rather than a factual account of Baal.

source_unit.text: Behold, the One guarding Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

target_units.text: At noon Elijah the Tishbite mocked them and said, “Call with a loud voice, for he is a god! He has chattering to do; perhaps he is also conducting business, or perhaps he is asleep and will get up!”

final_complete_triples.relationship: The Lord at the right hand
final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord will guard the addressee and is shelter at the right hand. Psalm 15 places the Lord at the speaker's right hand so that he may not be shaken. The divine position and protective result correspond, without adding shelter wording to Psalm 15.

source_unit.text: The Lord will guard you; the Lord is your shelter at your right hand.

target_units.text: I kept seeing the Lord before me continually, because He is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm promises that the sun will not scorch by day, alongside the moon by night. Isaiah promises that scorching heat and the sun will not strike those led by the merciful One. Protection from solar heat is shared; the moon clause remains particular to the psalm.

source_unit.text: By day the sun will not scorch you, nor the moon by night.

target_units.text: They will neither hunger nor thirst, nor will scorching heat or the sun strike them. Rather, the One showing them mercy will comfort them and lead them through springs of water.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord will guard the soul from all evil in the psalm. Jesus asks the Father to keep His disciples from the evil one in John. Both concern divine guarding against evil, while all evil and the evil one are retained as different expressions and scopes.

source_unit.text: The Lord will guard you from all evil; He will guard your soul.

target_units.text: I do not ask that Thou take them out of the world, but that Thou keep them from the evil one.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Coming in and going out under divine care
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm places coming in and going out under the Lord's perpetual guarding. Deuteronomy blesses the addressee when coming in and going out within its conditional covenant blessing. The paired movements correspond, without importing the psalm's duration into the target.

source_unit.text: The Lord will guard your coming in and your going out, from now and for ever.

target_units.text: Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The speaker recounts rejoicing over those who said they would go to the Lord's house. Isaiah portrays many nations inviting one another to go up to the Lord's mountain and the house of Jacob's God. Both concern a journey to God's house, with the reported resolve and the invitation distinguished.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. I rejoiced over those who said to me, “We will go to the Lord’s house.”

target_units.text: and many nations will go and say, “Come, let us go up to the Lord’s mountain and to the house of Jacob’s God. He will announce His way to us, and we will walk in it.” For law will go out from Zion, and the Lord’s word from Jerusalem.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Standing in the courts of God's house
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source locates the speakers' standing feet in Jerusalem's courts. Psalm 133 addresses those standing in the Lord's house and its courts. With the Lord's house already named in Psalm 121:1, both describe worshipers standing in the sacred courts.

source_unit.text: Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Behold, bless the Lord, all slaves of the Lord, who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Going up to the appointed place of worship
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm recounts the Lord's tribes going up to give thanks to His name. Deuteronomy requires the males to appear before the Lord at the chosen place on three annual feasts. The ascent for worship is compared with the prescribed gathering, without identifying the psalm's visit with one particular feast.

source_unit.text: for there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord—a testimony for Israel— to give thanks to the Lord’s name.

target_units.text: Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm places judgment thrones over David's house in Jerusalem. Jeremiah addresses the house of Judah's king and David's house, commanding morning judgment and rescue of the wronged. David's house and the duty of judgment connect the passages.

source_unit.text: For there thrones sat for judgment, thrones over David’s house.

target_units.text: House of Judah’s king, hear the Lord’s word.

House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The things belonging to Jerusalem's peace
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source asks for the things that bring Jerusalem peace. Jesus weeps over the city and speaks of the things that lead to peace that it failed to know. Jerusalem and its peace are particular to both, with the psalm's appeal and Jesus' lament kept distinct.

source_unit.text: Ask, then, for the things that bring Jerusalem peace, and prosperity for those who love you.

target_units.text: As He drew near and saw the city, He wept over it,
saying, “If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
For days will come upon you when your enemies will build a siege barrier around you and surround you and hem you in on every side.
They will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and will not leave stone upon stone within you, because you did not know the time of your visitation.”

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm wishes peace within Jerusalem's strength and prosperity within its fortified towers. Isaiah promises rulers in peace, the end of destruction within the borders, and walls called Salvation. Both associate the city's defenses with peace; Isaiah's walls and the psalm's towers are not treated as identical wording.

source_unit.text: May there be peace within your strength, and prosperity within your fortified towers.

target_units.text: Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, instead of iron silver, instead of wood bronze, and instead of stones iron. I will appoint your rulers in peace and your overseers in righteousness.
Injustice will no longer be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery within your borders. Your walls will be called Salvation, and your gates Engraving.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Lifting eyes toward heaven in prayer
final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the One dwelling in heaven. John describes Jesus lifting His eyes to heaven and addressing the Father. The bodily orientation of prayer is shared without identifying the prayers or their speakers.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. To Thee I lifted my eyes, Thou who dwellest in heaven.

target_units.text: Jesus spoke these things, and, lifting His eyes to heaven, said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Thy Son, so that the Son may glorify Thee,

final_complete_triples.rationale: The repeated request for mercy follows being filled with contempt. Nehemiah's prayer asks God to hear because the speakers have become objects of mockery. Both address God in response to communal contempt, without dating the psalm to the wall-building episode.

source_unit.text: Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with contempt to excess,

target_units.text: Hear, our God, for we have become an object of mockery. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them over to mockery in a land of captivity,

final_complete_triples.relationship: The call for Israel to speak
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both poems interrupt their opening recollection with the summons for Israel now to speak. Psalm 123 introduces a condition about the Lord's presence, whereas Psalm 128 introduces repeated hostility from youth. The shared congregational cue connects their forms.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. Had the Lord not been among us— let Israel now say—

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Many times they fought against me from my youth— let Israel now say—

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm considers what would have happened without the Lord among the speakers when people rose against them. Romans asks, if God is for us, who is against us. Both set divine support against human opposition, preserving the conditional retrospect and rhetorical question.

source_unit.text: had the Lord not been among us when people rose against us,

target_units.text: What, then, shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm describes hostile people conditionally swallowing the speakers alive. Proverbs quotes a murderous invitation to swallow a righteous man alive like Hades. The unusual image of swallowing a living victim connects the texts; the target's singular victim and Hades comparison remain distinct.

source_unit.text: then they would have swallowed us alive when their fury was kindled against us.

target_units.text: let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.

final_complete_triples.rationale: Within the opening conditional sequence, the source says water drowned the speakers and their soul passed through a torrent. Psalm 68 speaks of waters reaching the soul, entry into the sea's depths and a tempest drowning the speaker. The water-and-soul peril image corresponds without equating the afflictions.

source_unit.text: Then the water drowned us; our soul passed through a torrent.

target_units.text: Save me, God, for waters have entered as far as my soul.
I was stuck in the mud of the depth, with no firm ground; I entered the sea’s depths, and a tempest drowned me.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The soul's passage through irresistible water belongs to the psalm's condition about the Lord's presence. Isaiah joins crossing water with God's presence and a promise that rivers will not flood over Israel. Divine presence and passage through threatening waters connect the contrasting formulations.

source_unit.text: Then our soul passed through the irresistible water.

target_units.text: Even if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not flood over you. Even if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; flame will not burn you up.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm blesses the Lord for not giving the speakers as prey to enemies' teeth. Job recounts crushing unjust people's molars and tearing plunder from between their teeth. The shared predatory-teeth image links the Lord's withholding of prey and Job's removal of plunder, with their objects kept distinct.

source_unit.text: Blessed be the Lord, who did not give us as prey to their teeth.

target_units.text: I crushed the molars of unjust people and tore the plunder from between their teeth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A bird escaping a hunter's trap
final_complete_triples.rationale: The rescued soul is compared with a little bird escaping a shattered hunters' trap. Proverbs urges escape from a guarantor's danger like a bird from a trap. The bird-and-trap image is shared, while the psalm credits rescue and Proverbs gives an instruction.

source_unit.text: Our soul was rescued like a little bird from the trap of hunters; the trap was shattered, and we were rescued.

target_units.text: so that you may save yourself like a gazelle from snares and like a bird from a trap.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Help from the creator of heaven and earth
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source locates help in the name of the Lord who made heaven and earth. Psalm 120 likewise names the creator of heaven and earth as the source of help. The repeated formula connects the ascent songs while preserving the source's emphasis on the name.

source_unit.text: Our help is in the Lord’s name, who made heaven and earth.

target_units.text: My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The city and freedom from shaking
final_complete_triples.rationale: Those trusting in the Lord are compared with Mount Zion, and the Jerusalem dweller will never be shaken. Psalm 45 describes God's city as unshaken because God is in her midst. Both connect the city with freedom from shaking, but the source speaks of its dweller and the target of the city itself; the source also compares trusting people with Mount Zion.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. Those trusting in the Lord are like Mount Zion; the one dwelling in Jerusalem will never be shaken.

target_units.text: The river’s rushing streams gladden God’s city; the Most High sanctified His dwelling.
God is in her midst; she will not be shaken; God will help her toward morning.

final_complete_triples.rationale: Mountains around Jerusalem illustrate the Lord's surrounding His people. Zechariah promises that the Lord will be a wall of fire around Jerusalem and glory within her. Both use a surrounding defense to depict the Lord's protection, with mountains and a fiery wall distinguished.

source_unit.text: Mountains are around her, and the Lord is around His people, from now and for ever.

target_units.text: I will be a wall of fire around her, says the Lord, and I will be glory within her.”

final_complete_triples.rationale: The Lord will not leave sinners' rod upon the righteous person's lot. Isaiah says God shattered the sinners' and rulers' yoke. Both depict God ending sinful domination represented by an instrument of oppression; rod and yoke remain different images.

source_unit.text: For He will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the righteous, so that the righteous may not stretch out their hands in lawlessness.

target_units.text: God shattered the sinners’ yoke, the rulers’ yoke;

final_complete_triples.relationship: God's goodness to the upright in heart
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source asks the Lord to do good to the good and upright in heart. Psalm 72 declares God's goodness to Israel and to those upright in heart. Divine goodness and the same description of its recipients connect petition and declaration.

source_unit.text: Do good, Lord, to the good and to those upright in heart.

target_units.text: A psalm of Asaph. How good God is to Israel, to those upright in heart!

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source ends its judgment concerning tangled ways with peace upon Israel. Galatians pronounces peace and mercy upon those who will keep in step with its rule and upon the Israel of God. The explicit peace blessing connects the passages without equating their preceding judgments or defining their groups beyond the wording.

source_unit.text: But those turning aside into tangled ways— the Lord will lead them away with workers of lawlessness. Peace upon Israel.

target_units.text: And as many as will keep in step with this rule, peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm reports the Lord turning back Zion's captivity and the speakers becoming like those comforted. Jeremiah promises the return of Jacob's deportees, mercy on his captivity and rebuilding a city. Restoration from captivity connects report and promise without claiming one dated fulfillment.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.

target_units.text: Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will return Jacob’s deportees and have mercy on his captivity. A city will be built upon its height, and the sanctuary will sit according to its judgment.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm reports a mouth filled with joy and a tongue with exultation. Bildad forecasts God filling the mouth of true people with laughter and their lips with thanksgiving. The common image of a filled mouth is compared without endorsing Bildad's explanation of Job's suffering.

source_unit.text: Then our mouth was filled with joy and our tongue with exultation. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things with them.”

target_units.text: He will fill the mouth of true people with laughter, and their lips with thanksgiving.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source says the Lord has done great things with the speakers and they became glad. Mary says the Mighty One has done great things for her. The declaration of great divine acts is shared, with the communal and individual recipients distinguished.

source_unit.text: The Lord has done great things with us; we became glad.

target_units.text: because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is His name.

final_complete_triples.rationale: This same-chapter comparison places the petition to turn captivity beside the earlier report that the Lord turned Zion's captivity. The move from remembered restoration to a fresh request is explicit; the southern-torrent image is not supplied by the earlier unit.

source_unit.text: Turn back our captivity, Lord, like torrents in the south.

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. When the Lord turned back Zion’s captivity, we became like those comforted.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm promises joyful reaping for those sowing in tears. Galatians uses sowing and future reaping to encourage perseverance in doing good. The harvest image supports the comparison, while tears and exultation are not equated with Galatians' contrast between flesh and Spirit.

source_unit.text: Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.

target_units.text: For the one who sows into his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one who sows into the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
And let us not grow weary in doing good, for in the proper season we will reap, if we do not give up.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Same-chapter expansion of the sowing and reaping image
final_complete_triples.rationale: This same-chapter expansion gives the sowing-and-reaping saying a fuller scene: departure with tears and seeds, then expected arrival with exultation and sheaves. The neighboring unit states the pattern more briefly. Past going and weeping are preserved alongside future arrival.

source_unit.text: Going, they went and wept, carrying their seeds; but coming, they will arrive with exultation, carrying their sheaves.

target_units.text: Those sowing in tears will reap with exultation.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The heading associates the psalm with Solomon, and its opening makes successful building depend on the Lord. David tells Solomon that God is with him until he completes the ministry in the Lord's house. Solomon, building and divine aid connect the passages without restricting the psalm's house and city to the temple project.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. For Solomon. Unless the Lord builds a house, those building it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, the watchman has kept awake in vain.

target_units.text: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong, be of good courage, and act. Do not fear or be dismayed, for the Lord my God is with you. He will not let you go nor forsake you, until you finish all the work of ministry in the Lord’s house.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm describes vain exertion and bread of pain, then the sleep God gives His beloved ones. Ecclesiastes describes painful toil and a heart that does not sleep even at night. Labor, pain and lost or granted rest form the particular comparison.

source_unit.text: It is vain for you to rise early, to get up after sitting down, you who eat bread of pain, when He gives sleep to His beloved ones.

target_units.text: For what comes to a person from all his toil and the resolve of his heart with which he toils beneath the sun?
For all his days are pain, and his distraction is anger; even at night his heart does not sleep. This too is futility.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source calls sons the Lord's inheritance and the reward of the fruit of the womb. Jacob identifies his children as those with whom God has shown mercy to His servant. Both associate children with divine benefit, while the source's inheritance and reward remain its own terms.

source_unit.text: Behold, sons are the Lord’s inheritance, the reward of the fruit of the womb.

target_units.text: And he lifted up his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children with whom God has shown mercy to your servant.”

final_complete_triples.rationale: Sons of those who have been cast out are compared with arrows in a mighty man's hand. Isaiah's speaker describes being made a chosen arrow sheltered in God's quiver. People pictured as arrows connect the texts; neither the people nor the possessors of the arrows are equated.

source_unit.text: Like arrows in a mighty man’s hand, so are the sons of those who have been cast out.

target_units.text: and made my mouth like a sharp sword. In the shelter of His hand He hid me; He made me a chosen arrow and sheltered me in His quiver.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Fearing the Lord and walking in His ways
final_complete_triples.rationale: The beatitude joins fear of the Lord with walking in His ways. Deuteronomy likewise joins fearing the Lord and walking in all His ways among what He requires of Israel. The paired descriptions connect blessing and covenant instruction.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. Happy are all who fear the Lord, who walk in His ways.

target_units.text: And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to love Him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

final_complete_triples.relationship: Enjoying the fruit of one's own labor
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source promises eating the labors of one's wrists and being well. Isaiah describes people planting vineyards and eating their own produce, without others taking the benefit of their work. Enjoyment of one's own labor is the particular connection.

source_unit.text: You will eat the labors of your wrists; happy are you, and it will be well with you.

target_units.text: They will build houses and inhabit them themselves; they will plant vineyards and eat their own produce.
They will not build for others to inhabit or plant for others to eat. For My people’s days will be like those of the tree of life; they will wear out the works of their labor.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A woman compared with a fruitful vine
final_complete_triples.rationale: The wife is compared with a flourishing vine at the house. Ezekiel's lament over Israel's ruler compares the addressed person's mother with a vine planted by water. The woman-and-vine image is shared, while wife, mother and the lament's subsequent ruin remain distinct.

source_unit.text: Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.

target_units.text: Your mother was like a vine, like a blossom on a pomegranate tree, planted by water; her fruit and her shoot came from abundant water.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The sons are compared with newly planted olive trees around the table. Jeremiah describes the Lord naming the people a beautiful olive tree, then recounts its damaged branches. The comparison is limited to people represented as olive trees, with the family blessing and judgment scene distinguished.

source_unit.text: Your wife is like a flourishing vine in the sides of your house; your sons are like newly planted olive trees around your table.

target_units.text: The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, well-shaded in appearance. At the sound of its pruning, fire was kindled upon it; great is the affliction upon you, and its branches became useless.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The blessed person who fears the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both describe the blessed person through fear of the Lord. Psalm 127 summarizes the household blessing in its surrounding units, while Psalm 111 begins a beatitude and adds delight in the commandments. The explicit fear-and-blessing formula is shared.

source_unit.text: Behold, thus will the person be blessed who fears the Lord.

target_units.text: Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will greatly delight in His commandments.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source wishes for the Lord's blessing from Zion, while Psalm 133 declares that He will bless from Zion. Psalm 127 additionally wishes that the person see Jerusalem's good things through life; Psalm 133 additionally identifies the Lord as maker of heaven and earth. The shared blessing formula remains precise.

source_unit.text: May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see Jerusalem’s good things all the days of your life.

target_units.text: The Lord will bless you from Zion, who made heaven and earth.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source wishes that the addressee see sons of his sons. Job's conclusion reports that he saw his sons and his sons' sons, a fourth generation. The experience of seeing descendants connects wish and narrative; Job's stated lifespan is not transferred to the psalm.

source_unit.text: And may you see sons of your sons. Peace upon Israel.

target_units.text: After the affliction, Job lived one hundred seventy years; in all, he lived two hundred forty-eight years. Job saw his sons and his sons’ sons, a fourth generation.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The summons for Israel to speak
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both openings summon Israel now to speak within a recollection of danger. Psalm 128 recalls repeated fighting from youth, while Psalm 123 asks what would have happened without the Lord's presence. The particular congregational summons connects the songs.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. Many times they fought against me from my youth— let Israel now say—

target_units.text: A song of the ascents. Had the Lord not been among us— let Israel now say—

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source reports repeated fighting in which the opponents did not prevail. God tells Jeremiah that people will fight him but will certainly not prevail, because He is with him to rescue him. The paired fighting-and-not-prevailing language connects communal report and prophetic assurance.

source_unit.text: many times they fought against me from my youth, and indeed they did not prevail over me.

target_units.text: and they will fight you, but they will certainly not prevail against you, because I am with you to rescue you, said the Lord.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Hostile acts against the speaker's back
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source places sinners' work on the speaker's back and describes prolonged lawlessness. Isaiah's speaker gives his back to scourges. The location of hostile action on the back is shared; plowing or furrows are not imported into the supplied psalm.

source_unit.text: On my back sinners worked; they prolonged their lawlessness.

target_units.text: I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps. I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Shame and turning back for enemies
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both wish shame and a backward turning upon adversaries. Psalm 128 identifies them as those hating Zion; Psalm 34 identifies them as those seeking the speaker's soul and devising evils. The paired outcomes connect distinct descriptions of enemies.

source_unit.text: May all who hate Zion be put to shame and turn backward.

target_units.text: Let those who seek my soul be ashamed and abashed; let those devising evils for me turn backward and be put to shame.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Rooftop grass as an image of weakness
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source wishes Zion's enemies to become rooftop grass that dried up before it was pulled out. The oracle concerning Sennacherib compares weakened city inhabitants with rooftop grass among other images. The unusual rooftop-grass comparison is shared, with different subjects and the psalm's drying clause preserved.

source_unit.text: May they become like grass on roofs, which dried up before it was pulled out,

target_units.text: Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed. They became field grass or green herbage, rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.

final_complete_triples.relationship: A contrasting blessing at the harvest
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source says passersby have not spoken the divine blessing, following the barren grass image. Ruth narrates Boaz greeting reapers with the Lord's presence and their reply asking the Lord to bless him. The harvest setting and divine blessing create a contrast between an absent greeting and an exchanged one.

source_unit.text: And passersby have not said, “The Lord’s blessing be upon you; we have blessed you in the Lord’s name.”

target_units.text: And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “The Lord be with you.” They said to him, “May the Lord bless you.”

final_complete_triples.rationale: The psalm cries to the Lord from the depths. Jonah's prayer combines crying from the belly of Hades with being cast into the sea's depths. The cry from a depth of peril connects the prayers without identifying their occasions.

source_unit.text: A song of the ascents. From the depths I have cried unto Thee, Lord.

target_units.text: and said: “In my affliction I cried to the Lord my God, and He listened to me. From the belly of Hades Thou didst hear the voice of my cry.
Thou didst cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers encircled me. All Thy billows and Thy waves passed over me.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source asks that the Lord's ears attend to the voice of petition. Solomon asks that God's ears be attentive to the supplication of this place. The attentive-ear prayer formula is shared; the temple location belongs to Solomon's prayer.

source_unit.text: Lord, hear my voice; let Thine ears be attentive to the voice of my petition.

target_units.text: Now, O Lord, I beseech Thee, let Thine eyes be open, and Thine ears attentive to the supplication of this place.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Who can stand with lawless deeds
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source asks who could withstand if the Lord closely watched lawless deeds. Ezra's confession says there is no standing before God because of the people's offenses. Lawless conduct and inability to stand before God connect question and confession.

source_unit.text: If Thou dost closely watch lawless deeds, Lord, Lord, who will withstand?

target_units.text: Lord, God of Israel, Thou art righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as on this day. Here we are before Thee in our offenses, for because of this there is no standing before Thee.”

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source says atonement is with the Lord. Psalm 64 says God will make atonement for the speakers' impieties after words of lawless deeds overpowered them. The shared atonement claim connects both passages' response to lawlessness.

source_unit.text: For with Thee is atonement.

target_units.text: Words of lawless deeds overpowered us, and Thou wilt make atonement for our impieties.

final_complete_triples.relationship: The soul waiting for God's word
final_complete_triples.rationale: The source speaks of waiting for the Lord and His word. Psalm 118 describes the soul failing with longing for salvation and hope placed in God's word. Waiting and hoping are distinguished, while the soul's dependence on the divine word is particular to both.

source_unit.text: Because of Thy law I waited for Thee, Lord; my soul waited for Thy word.

target_units.text: Eleven: Chaph. My soul fails with longing for Thy salvation, and I placed my hope in Thy word.

final_complete_triples.relationship: Israel exhorted to hope in the Lord
final_complete_triples.rationale: Both expressly call Israel to hope in the Lord. Psalm 129 frames the call with the soul's hope from the morning watch until night; Psalm 130 extends the communal exhortation from now and for ever. The temporal forms are preserved.

source_unit.text: My soul hoped in the Lord from the morning watch until night; from the morning watch let Israel hope in the Lord.

target_units.text: Let Israel hope in the Lord, from now and for ever.

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source joins the Lord's mercy with abundant redemption. Ephesians describes redemption through Christ's blood according to the riches of His grace. Redemptive provision and its abundance connect the passages, while blood and forgiveness are explicit features of Ephesians.

source_unit.text: For with the Lord is mercy, and with Him is abundant redemption,

target_units.text: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of transgressions, according to the riches of His grace,

final_complete_triples.rationale: The source says He will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds. Titus describes Christ giving Himself to ransom us from all lawlessness. The redemptive action and comprehensive lawlessness clause correspond, with Israel, us and Christ's self-giving kept as the respective texts state them.

source_unit.text: And He will redeem Israel from all its lawless deeds.
